metadata.summary: Background: The molecular mechanisms underlying heart failure (HF) following myocardial infarction (MI) (HF-MI) remain incompletely understood, and whole-transcriptome profiling studies hold significant promise for disease prevention and treatment. Methods: Whole-transcriptome sequencing was performed on post-MI patients with and without HF to analyze differentially expressed mRNAs, lncRNAs, and circRNAs, along with functional enrichment analysis. Co-expression networks linking lncRNA-mRNA and circRNA-mRNA pairs, as well as ceRNA networks involving lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA and circRNA-miRNA-mRNA interactions, were constructed for differentially expressed (DE) RNAs. Key lncRNAs were validated by RT-qPCR. Transcriptional factor-lncRNA networks were constructed, and key relationships were verified using RIP-PCR. Results: Patients with HF-MI exhibited marked elevation of NT-proBNP and significant reduction in LVEF%. Transcriptome-wide analysis revealed 228 DE-mRNAs, 700 DE-lncRNAs, and 1188 DE-circRNAs in HF-MI compared to non-heart failure patients (NHF-MI). Construction of the ceRNA network identified hsa-miR-6089 and hsa-miR-6771-5p as key miRNAs in the lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA network, while hsa-miR-1207-5p and hsa-miR-10392-3p were key miRNAs in the circRNA-miRNA-mRNA network. PVT1, SNHG5, TTN-AS1, HCP5, and OIP5-AS1 were identified as the five key DE-lncRNAs, with PVT1/SNHG5 showing upregulation and TTN-AS1/HCP5/OIP5-AS1 exhibiting downregulation. The transcription factor-lncRNA network primarily involves GLIS3-HCP5 and ZNF135-PVT1, with validated associative interactions. Conclusion: This study systematically mapped the regulatory network of HF-MI, revealing the roles of the GLIS3-HCP5 and ZNF135-PVT1 regulatory axes in HF-MI, thereby providing a basis for exploring novel therapeutic strategies.

observations.title: Transcriptome Expression Profiles and Regulatory Networks in Patients with Heart Failure Following Myocardial Infarction

metadata.summary: Oncofetal programs are often co-opted in high-grade gliomas and represent tumor cell vulnerabilities for therapeutic exploitation. Here, we integrate single nucleus RNA-seq and single-cell ATAC sequencing data generated from germinal matrix and cortical plate regions macrodissected from prenatal and postnatal developing brain autopsy tissue, creating an expanded spatiotemporal multi-omic dataset of gliogenic progenitors. The integrated multi-omics data includes previously published data (Ramos et al, Nature Commun 2022; Herring et al, Cell 2022) as well as newly-generated and herein deposited data. We use this dataset to interrogate oncofetal cell state composition in grade 4 gliomas across several published high-grade glioma / glioblastoma (GBM) datasets to uniquely assess tumor heterogeneity related to infiltrative biology near the margin and disease recurrence, in addition to genomic drivers. Our analyses reveal the preferential enrichment of glial intermediate progenitor cell (gIPC)-like cell state in GBM, most reminiscent of third-trimester germinal matrix gIPC progenitors, across tumor regions and in recurrence, irrespective of EGFR amplification status.

metadata.summary: Background: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) followed by a reperfusion results in a phasic response by cardiac macrophages. During the first 7 days after AMI, macrophage populations exhibit dynamic phenotypic changes. Ultimately, inflammatory damage results in ventricular remodeling and fibrosis. Macrophages are critical to cardiac function and long-term prognoses. Objective: Elucidate the spatiotemporal behavior of specific macrophage subtypes during  AMI and identify novel genes with prospective therapeutic potential. Methods: We implement an IRI mouse model of AMI to assess cardiac macrophage behavior during AMI. RCM were isolated using flow cytometry and analyzed with NanoString. Pathway enrichment analysis annotated statistically significant genes. We employed transcriptome-wide, spatiotemporal analysis of cardiac tissue samples during  AMI.

observations.text:
BackgroundCross-cohort machine-learning studies of tau positivity are increasingly used to assess generalizability of Alzheimers disease biomarker models, but apparent differences between cohorts may reflect clinical severity structure and cohort stage composition rather than genuine biological divergence.

MethodsWe evaluated this problem across subject-level cohorts from the Alzheimers Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), the Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (OASIS3), and the National Alzheimers Coordinating Center (NACC) using harmonized tabular predictors and a feature-block ablation framework. For ADNI and OASIS3, we performed matched-feature analyses restricted to shared harmonized variables (age, APOE{varepsilon} 4, education, sex, the CDR(R) Dementia Staging Instrument sum-of-boxes score (CDR-SB), and the Functional Activities Questionnaire (FAQ)). Models were trained with five-fold stratified cross-validation using balanced logistic regression as the primary classifier. Random forests and extra-trees classifiers were evaluated as robustness checks and are reported in supplementary analyses.

ResultsIn the primary matched-feature comparison, reference areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) were 0.851 for ADNI tau90, 0.860 for ADNI tau180, and 0.933 for OASIS3 tau180. Severity-only models retained 86-99% of reference performance, whereas demographic/genetic-only models retained 85-87%; bootstrap confidence intervals showed that the reference-minus-demo contrast remained positive across all primary cohorts. Before feature matching, OASIS3 showed substantially weaker demographic-only prediction (AUC{approx} 0.54), attributable to missing APOE and age variables. After harmonization with a matched feature set including age, the pre-harmonization demographic gap was no longer attributable to feature availability; the residual difference was most consistent with cohort disease-stage composition asymmetry, with CDR-SB = 0 prevalence of 84.5-88.7% in OASIS3 versus 49.3-51.7% in ADNI.

ConclusionsThe original large ADNI-OASIS3 performance gap was largely a feature-availability artifact; after strict harmonization including age-field repair, the absolute gap narrowed and the signed ADNI-minus-OASIS3 difference reversed, with the residual difference most consistent with cohort disease-stage composition asymmetry. Clinical severity remains an important predictor across all cohorts, but the unique contributions of severity and demographic/genetic information depend strongly on stage composition. Cross-cohort biomarker modeling should account for both feature-set completeness and disease-stage composition heterogeneity, not only headline performance metrics.
observations.title: Feature harmonization reveals that apparent cross-cohort differences in tau-positivity prediction reflect variable availability and cohort stage structure

observations.text: Existing supervised and self-supervised EEG models mainly learn within-segment discriminative or reconstructive representations, leaving transitions between adjacent EEG segments underexplored. We propose a self-supervised Multimodal EEG World Model for EEG seizure detection that predicts the latent representation of the next EEG segment from the current EEG state, conditioned on synchronized ECG, EMG, and movement signals. A learnable query-based fusion module aggregates the multimodal synchronized signals into a compact physiological condition. Pretraining uses no seizure labels; downstream detection retains only the frozen EEG encoder and a linear probe. On the SeizeIT2 dataset with a strict patient-wise split, the model achieved an AUPRC of 0.3748{+/-}0.0127, ROC-AUC of 0.8025{+/-}0.0071, and balanced accuracy of 0.7308{+/-}0.0075, outperforming official database baseline (SVM with hand-crafted features, ChronoNet), external baselines (DSAINet) and foundation models (NeuroLM). Ablations show a 14.4% relative AUPRC gain over a random-initialized encoder, supporting multimodal-conditioned latent transition learning for wearable EEG representation learning.
observations.title: MULTIMODAL EEG WORLD MODEL: SELF-SUPERVISED LATENT TRANSITION LEARNING FOR WEARABLE EEG SEIZURE DETECTION

metadata.summary: Myocardial infarction (MI) causes cardiomyocyte loss and fibrotic scar formation, disrupting electrical communication and impairing cardiac function. Conductive hydrogels have been studied to reconstruct an electroactive microenvironment for the infarcted myocardium, yet their regenerative effect is limited by the impaired function of surviving cardiomyocytes. Here, we developed a mechanoelectrically active and paintable hydrogel capable of converting cardiac motion into localized electrical stimulation to repair infarcted myocardium. The paintable nature of the hydrogel enables easy application onto irregular epicardial surfaces using a customized brush, while subsequent photocrosslinking allows selective adhesion of the hydrogel to only epicardial surfaces, not to surrounding tissues. Under cyclic loading and in contracting cardiac organoids, the hydrogel generated physiologically relevant electrical potentials, demonstrating efficient deformation-induced charge generation. In a rat MI model, the hydrogel providing electrostimulation alleviated ventricular wall thinning and fibrosis, promoted neovascularization and M2 macrophage polarization, and improved cardiac function. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed upregulation of genes involved in myocardial contraction and energy metabolism. As such, our study offers a minimally invasive and clinically translatable approach for cardiac repair and other tissue applications.

observations.text: Patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) often are excluded from receiving CMR scans at 3.0T due to ICD-induced image artifacts. This work aims to transfer sequence protocols established for CMR imaging in the presence of ICDs at 1.5T to a first human application at 3.0T. All measurements were performed on a clinical 3T MRI scanner. Phantom measurements were used to establish and optimize wideband PSIR LGE imaging at 3.0T. Volunteer measurements with externally placed ICDs were used for optimization of CINE imaging and wideband PSIR imaging. Thirdly, patients with implanted ICD were examined with the optimized protocols. Human measurements showed that SA stacks obtained with spoiled GRE after contrast agent showed a markedly lower artifact burden than the conventional approach. For scar imaging, a wideband PSIR with a bandwidth of 3kHz and a frequency offset of +750Hz allowed a sufficient suppression of relevant artifacts in the majority of scans. No strong correlation between the image quality and the distance between the cardiac silhouette and the device was detected. The presented work shows the feasibility of clinical cardiac MRI at 3.0T including GRE-CINE and wideband PSIR-LGE for patients with ICDs.
observations.title: Cardiac MRI at 3.0T in the presence of implantable cardioverter defibrillators (ICDs)

metadata.summary: This study generated a transcriptome-wide resource of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) from two clinical groups: subjects with hyperuricemia (HUA, n=15) and subjects with coronary artery disease together with hyperuricemia (CHD_HUA, n=15). Total RNA was extracted from PBMC and poly(A)+ mRNA was enriched with oligo(dT) magnetic beads. Strand-specific libraries were constructed using dUTP incorporation and UDG second-strand digestion, and paired-end 150 bp sequencing was performed on an Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Clean reads were aligned to the Homo sapiens reference genome with HISAT2, and transcripts were assembled and quantified with StringTie. Gene-level raw read counts and FPKM values for all 30 samples are provided as processed data, together with the paired-end FASTQ files. The dataset is intended to support investigation of transcriptional differences between hyperuricemia and coronary artery disease with hyperuricemia.

metadata.summary: Obesity-induced metabolic cardiomyopathy features myocardial lipid overload, mitochondrial dysfunction and chronic inflammation, with few targeted therapies. Hyodeoxycholic acid (HDCA), a natural secondary bile acid, plays key roles in metabolic homeostasis, yet its direct cardioprotective effects in obesity-related cardiac injury remain unclear. Here, we investigated HDCA effects on high-fat diet-induced cardiomyopathy using in vivo, lipotoxic cardiomyocyte and 3D cardiac spheroid models. HDCA ameliorated cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophic remodeling and myocardial lipid accumulation. Transcriptomics showed HDCA remodelled cardiac programs governing mitochondrial and lipid metabolism as well as inflammation. Mechanistically, HDCA limited cardiomyocyte lipid uptake via TGR5-dependent suppression of CD36 membrane localization, boosted mitochondrial respiration and ATP production, and reduced oxidative stress. HDCA also bound PIK3CA to inhibit PI3K-AKT-mediated inflammation. In 3D cardiac spheroids, HDCA alleviated lipotoxic injury. Collectively, HDCA protects against obesity-associated cardiomyopathy by coordinating myocardial lipid metabolism, mitochondrial homeostasis and inflammatory signaling, representing a promising candidate for metabolic heart disease.

observations.title: Hyodeoxycholic acid protects against obesity-associated cardiomyopathy by restoring myocardial metabolic homeostasis and suppressing inflammatory remodeling

metadata.summary: Laminopathies comprise a diverse array of phenotypes that involve multiple organs and are caused by mutations in the LMNA gene, which encodes nuclear envelope protein lamin A (LMNA). Cardiac involvement is a prominent feature and a major cause of mortality and morbidity in laminopathies. LMNA interacts with chromatin through lamin-associated domains (LADs) and regulates gene expression. The role of the LMNA in regulating chromatin structure and gene expression in cardiac myocytes is unknown.  We conditionally deleted the Lmna gene specifically in cardiac myocytes in the mouse, isolated the LMNA-deficient cardiac myocytes, and characterized genomic structure and function at two levels: first, by identifying and characterizing the genome-wide CTCF binding sites by a CUT&RUN assay; and second, the chromatin conformational changes by HiC.  To determine the role of LMNA in genome organization and gene expression we integrated CTCF binding, LAD, Hi-C data with the gene expression (RNA-seq), and DNA double-stranded breaks (DSBs), determined by END-Seq, in cardiac myocytes.  Compared to wild-type (WT) myocytes, LMNA deficiency increased genomic occupancy of CTCF , predominantly outside of the constitutive LADs (cLADs), and increased gene expression at the CTCF binding sites. Likewise, DSBs were highly enriched at the CTCF binding sites. However, only a small fraction of the chromatin compartments was shifted in the LMNA-deficient cardiac myocytes. LMNA-deficiency changed the organization of one-third of the topologically-associated domains (TADs). The changes were characterized by the merger of 2 or more TADs (60%), mainly in the non-LAD regions, splitting (30%), and shifting boundaries (10%). Reorganization of TADs, however, did not directly affect gene expression or the prevalence of DSBs. A remarkable effect of the LMNA deficiency was on chromatin loops, as it led to a gain of ~ 600 and a loss of ~1000 loops, whose boundaries were enriched in the CTCF binding sites. The changes affected the transcript level of ~25% of the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the LMNA-deficient cardiac myocytes. The gain of the loop was associated with increased gene expression, whereas the loss of the loop had the opposite effect. A multivariate analysis showed that differential CTCF  binding  (largest), loops, and cLADs affected the transcript levels of the DEGs, whereas TADs and chromatin compartments appeared to act in concert with these factors  rather than as independent determinants.  In conclusion, LMNA regulates chromatin structure like TADs its role in  gene expression is mediated mainly through CTCF, cLADs, and loops,. The findings provide insights into the molecular pathogenesis of cardiac involvement in the diverse array of phenotypes in laminopathies.

observations.title: Effects of the Lamin A on Chromatin Structure and Function in Cardiac Myocytes in a Mouse Model of Lamin-Cardiomyopathy

metadata.summary: Truncating variants in desmoplakin (DSP) are a leading cause of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, a severe heart muscle disease characterized by fibrosis and life-threatening arrhythmias. Desmoplakin anchors the junctions that hold heart muscle cells together to the internal cytoskeleton, enabling the heart to withstand the force of each contraction. No targeted therapy exists, and DSP is too large for conventional gene replacement. Here we show, in explanted human hearts and in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes, that truncating DSP variants reduce desmoplakin RNA and protein, and that the resulting haploinsufficiency renders cardiomyocytes vulnerable to cell–cell adhesion failure under contractile stress, preceded by disruption of the cell membrane. Lowering contractile force with the myosin inhibitor mavacamten prevents this failure. Circumventing the size of DSP, CRISPR-based transcriptional activation of the endogenous gene restores desmoplakin expression and rescues adhesion. Haploinsufficiency is therefore the primary defect in DSP cardiomyopathy, and transcriptional activation offers a therapeutic strategy.

metadata.summary: Diabetic cardiomyopathy is a clinical condition of ventricular dysfunction, with obesity and insulin resistance as the primary risk factors. Under this condition, the heart accumulates fatty acids and encounters lipotoxicity, which impairs cardiac insulin sensitivity and leads to cardiomyopathy. Angiotensin-(1-9) is a peptide of the counter-regulatory axis of the renin-angiotensin system with cardioprotective effects in myocardial infarction. However, its role in diabetic cardiomyopathy is unknown. To explore the role of angiotensin-(1-9), we first induced lipotoxic stress in the heart by high-fat diet (HFD) feeding in mice. Angiotensin-(1-9) was then administered for four weeks using osmotic mini-pumps. Cardiac function was assessed by, and insulin sensitivity was evaluated in tissues after a bolus of insulin injection. Moreover, lipotoxic stress in vitro was modeled by high glucose medium plus palmitate in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes (NRVMs). We show that angiotensin-(1-9) improves myocardial function and reverts pathological cardiac remodeling in mice. Moreover, angiotensin-(1-9) enhances whole-body glucose tolerance and reduces homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR). We next demonstrate that angiotensin-(1-9) increases insulin sensitivity in the heart and skeletal muscle but not in adipose tissue or the liver. Mechanistically, angiotensin-(1-9) does not affect insulin signaling in cardiomyocytes at baseline, while it significantly improves insulin action under lipotoxic stress through AT2 receptor (AT2R) and PKA. These findings demonstrate that angiotensin-(1-9) improves cardiac function under metabolic challenge and promotes insulin signaling in cardiomyocytes under lipotoxicity, which may shed light on the therapeutic exploration against diabetic cardiomyopathy.

observations.title: Angiotensin-(1-9) protects cardiomyocytes under lipotoxic stress by AT2 receptor

observations.text: Alzheimer's disease (AD) staging based on amyloid-{beta}, tau, and neurodegeneration does not capture heterogeneous microglial functions. Existing transcriptomic scores indicate microglial activation or state similarity but do not resolve post-activation functions and are not directly comparable across scales. Herein, we develop a function-oriented framework comprising seven harmful-and seven adaptive-associated gene modules, selected from predefined mechanisms and direct functional evidence. Using SEA-AD micro-glia/perivascular macrophage nuclei, we compute do-nor-brain-region pseudobulk scores on a fixed P10-P90 reference scale and validate them against matched protein, activity, and tissue endpoints. H3 is related to cytokine/chemokine proteins; H4 and A5 are related to the same isoprostane readout in opposite directions; and A3 is related to dense-core plaque fraction. Benchmark comparison shows modest incremental fit but distinct out-come-specific information. In external GSE146639, eight modules remained FDR-significant, although harmful and adaptive arms are highly collinear; H7 and A2 are replicated in external proteomics. Downsampling, leave-one-gene-out, and alternative scoring analyses supports technical stability, and single-cell reconstruction supported a state-resolved basis. These scores summarize relative engagement of damage-related and adaptive programmes, enabling mechanistic comparison across donors and brain regions, but remain observational, are not intended for clinical decision-making, and require further validation.
observations.title: Function-oriented microglial transcriptional scores in Alz-heimer's disease: resolving terminal functions beyond activa-tion states

metadata.summary: IRAG1 is well-established regulator of intracellular Ca2+ signaling and smooth muscle cell relaxation. Through integrative analysis of multiple omics datasets, we identified IRAG1 as a candidate effector gene at a coronary artery disease-associated risk locus.  IRAG1 expression is enriched in differentiated vascular smooth muscle cells and markedly reduced during smooth muscle cell phenotypic modulation in atherosclerosis. To further investigate the function of IRAG1 in vascular smooth muscle cells, we performed siRNA-mediated knockdown of IRAG1 in human coronary artery smooth muscle cells (HCASMCs), followed by bulk RNA-seq 48 hours after transfection. Differential gene analysis revealed that IRAG1 knockdown induced transcriptional programs associated with proliferation and inflammatory responses.

metadata.summary: Background: Reactive oxygen species are increased across most pulmonary hypertension (PH) etiologies, resulting in increased reactive lipid dicarbonyls, which form protein adducts and impair mitochondrial function. We hypothesized that reducing reactive lipids would reduce right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP) and improve cardiac function by eliminating protein-lipid damage feedback loops. Methods: We used 2-hydroxybenzylamine (2-HOBA) to scavenge reactive lipids in three complimentary mouse models of PH: AKR-high fat diet (HFD, metabolic stress), LNAME-HFD (cardiometabolic syndrome), and pulmonary artery banding (PAB, load stress). Cardiac function was measured by echocardiography and catheterization. RV energy metabolism was determined by oxygraphy. Mass spectrometry analyzed lipids and ceramides; O-link and RNA-Seq evaluated proteomic and gene expression in lungs, RV, and LV. Results: Reducing reactive lipids with 2-HOBA resulted in a ~10% reduction in RVSP, reduced diastolic dysfunction, reduced plasma lipids and ceramides, and normalized RV fatty acid oxidation that was severely impaired in the AKR-HFD and PAB models. Proteomic and RNA changes in the lungs, RV, and LV suggested reduced oxidative damage and inflammatory signaling and altered developmental and actin organization signaling; these changes are plausibly associated with the improved adaptation. Some changes were sex specific, including a 4x higher cardiac fatty acid content in males than females. Conclusions: Reactive lipid scavenging improves cardiac metabolic and diastolic function and pulmonary vascular resistance through restoration of mitochondrial function and reduced oxidative protein damage. The magnitude of hemodynamic improvement combined with substantial diastolic function improvement suggests clinical potential, particularly for PH patients with metabolic comorbidities.

observations.title: Reducing Reactive Lipids Improves Cardiac Metabolic and Diastolic Function in Pulmonary Hypertension Models

observations.text:
IntroductionOverall survival (OS) is the gold standard for demonstrating treatment benefit in oncology but requires prolonged follow-up. Surrogate efficacy endpoints, such as progression-free survival, can shorten trial duration and reduce costs but may not consistently reflect overall survival benefit. We hypothesized that integrating patient-reported outcomes (PROs) with surrogate endpoints would improve trial-level prediction of OS benefit.

MethodsWe reviewed clinical trials supporting FDA oncology drug approvals from 2013 to 2023 that reported OS, at least one surrogate efficacy endpoint, and PROs. Machine learning models predicted OS benefit were developed using surrogate endpoints alone or surrogate endpoint features combined with PROs. Both models were validated using repeated five-fold trial-grouped cross-validation and leave-one-trial-out validation.

ResultsA total of 100 clinical trials (103 between-arm comparisons, 68,987 participants) met inclusion criteria. Compared with control arms, 68% of active treatment arms demonstrated OS benefit, 83.5% showed surrogate endpoints improvement, and 35.9% showed improvement in PROs. Adding PROs to machine learning models increased area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) from 0.67 (95% CI, 0.55-0.78) to 0.79 (95% CI, 0.69-0.87), an absolute increase of 0.12 indicating improved model discrimination. Leave-one-trial-out validation confirmed the improvement (AUC-ROC, 0.663 versus 0.795; paired difference, 0.132; 95% CI, 0.017-0.248).

ConclusionsIntegrating PROs with surrogate endpoints improved prediction of OS benefit, supporting machine learning as a quantitative framework for combining complementary endpoints in oncology drug development.

metadata.summary: Reperfusion of ischemic myocardium triggers a sterile inflammatory cascade in which NF-κB–dependent transcriptional priming precedes NLRP3 inflammasome assembly and caspase-1 activation. Diacerein, approved for osteoarthritis, is converted in vivo to rhein, an NF-κB inhibitor with inflammasome-attenuating properties, but its effect on the ischemic myocardial transcriptome is unknown.  To define the transcriptional program underlying diacerein-mediated cardioprotection, male Wistar rats received oral diacerein (80 mg/kg/day) or vehicle for 10 days before the heart was isolated and subjected to global no-flow ischemia followed by reperfusion in a Langendorff preparation. RNA sequencing of left ventricular tissue identified 314 differentially expressed genes (268 downregulated, 46 upregulated) in diacerein- versus vehicle-treated hearts. Downregulated genes included Selp (P-selectin), the endothelial adhesion molecule mediating leukocyte capture, Csf2rb (the shared GM-CSF/IL-3/IL-5 receptor subunit), and Ripk1, while Card9 was upregulated. Gene set enrichment analysis showed suppression of TNF signaling, NF-κB signaling, and cytokine–cytokine receptor interaction pathways.  These data indicate that diacerein pretreatment suppresses leukocyte recruitment and inflammatory priming programs in the ischemic myocardium, and provide a transcriptional basis for its cardioprotective effect.

observations.text: Background: Protein-protein interactions govern essential cellular processes, making the identification of interface residues critical for protein engineering and molecular design. Although complex deep learning algorithms like AlphaFold3 generate full atom resolution assemblies, they are not optimized for residue-level interface identification. Existing methods face inherent limitations: sequence-based models lack explicit 3D context, while structure-based approaches can overlook evolutionary signals. Results: By combining evolutionary context with 3D geometry, the multimodal protein language model ESM3 offers the ideal foundation for residue-level interface classification. This results in the ESM3-PPISites model, which outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods across diverse training and benchmark sets. Generalization is assessed through stringent sequence- and structure-based redundancy filtering to ensure evaluation on previously unseen proteins. Notably, finetuning the open-weight ESM3 architecture meaningfully narrows the performance gap with its proprietary full-scale counterpart. Furthermore, integrating predicted interaction sites as spatial restraints into HADDOCK significantly improves the recovery of near-native binding poses while reducing computational search time by an order of magnitude compared with blind docking. Conclusions: ESM3-PPISites enables accurate interfaces identification without relying on complex structural inputs at inference time, establishing a reliable and computationally efficient strategy for mapping protein-protein interaction sites.
observations.title: Learning Protein-Protein Interaction Interfaces from Multimodal Representations

observations.text: Biological neural systems learn new behaviors while retaining earlier ones, whereas sequentially trained artificial networks often overwrite parameters and forget previously learned behaviors. We introduce the Context-modulated Synaptic-states Recurrent Neural Network (CoSyn-RNN), a new continual-learning model inspired by heterogeneous synaptic states and neuromodulatory control. CoSyn-RNN combines sparse recurrent allocation with a discrete protection rule: after each task, recurrent neurons whose synaptic weights cross a fixed threshold form a task-specific neuron group, and their associated parameters enter a protected state during later learning. A neuron-specific gain and a task-cued mask over a fixed base readout control how recurrent activity contributes to behavior. Across various task sequences consisting of many cognitive tasks, training and validation losses and accuracies were maintained throughout learning. The protection rule produced modular, task-ordered recurrent structure compatible with forward reuse of earlier computations. Pairwise recruitment measurements further defined minimum- and maximum-cost curricula that produced markedly different final recurrent structures and different remaining capacity for future learning. Thus, CoSyn-RNN provides a biologically inspired model in which protected synaptic states, sparse allocation, and context-dependent modulation support continual learning.

metadata.summary: Oncofetal programs are often co-opted in high-grade gliomas and represent tumor cell vulnerabilities for therapeutic exploitation. Here, we integrate single nucleus RNA-seq and single-cell ATAC sequencing data generated from germinal matrix and cortical plate regions macrodissected from prenatal and postnatal developing brain autopsy tissue, creating an expanded spatiotemporal multi-omic dataset of gliogenic progenitors. The integrated multi-omics data includes previously published data (Ramos et al, Nature Commun 2022; Herring et al, Cell 2022) as well as newly-generated and herein deposited data. We use this dataset to interrogate oncofetal cell state composition in grade 4 gliomas across several published high-grade glioma / glioblastoma (GBM) datasets to uniquely assess tumor heterogeneity related to infiltrative biology near the margin and disease recurrence, in addition to genomic drivers. Our analyses reveal the preferential enrichment of glial intermediate progenitor cell (gIPC)-like cell state in GBM, most reminiscent of third-trimester germinal matrix gIPC progenitors, across tumor regions and in recurrence, irrespective of EGFR amplification status.

metadata.summary: Nuclear receptor subfamily 4 group A member 2 (NR4A2) is a widely expressed immediate early gene induced by a host of physiological signals such as growth factors, cytokines, and neurotransmitters. In the adult mammalian heart, including in cardiomyocytes, NR4A2 mRNAs increase more than 60-fold in response to beta-adrenergic stimulation. However, the nature of the transcriptional remodeling induced by NR4A2 in the stressed heart has remained poorly investigated. We show here that NR4A2 activation in mouse cardiomyocytes leads to a rapid remodeling of the cardiac microRNA network. A total of 35 miRNAs were down-regulated, including the muscle-specific miR-133a and miR-499. On the opposite, 65 miRNAs were up-regulated, with a strong representation of miRNAs encoded within the imprinted Dlk1-Dio3 domain. Non-coding RNAs from the Dlk1-Dio3 locus are known for coordinating critical steps of cardiac development such as cardiac lineage commitment, cardiac morphogenesis, and cardiomyocyte proliferation, and for inhibiting mitochondrial function in myocytes. The findings shed light on a novel regulatory mechanism controlling cardiac homeostasis, and establish a framework to investigate further the roles played by NR4A2 in cardiac adaptation or maladaptation to various acute and pathological stress conditions.

metadata.summary: Truncating variants in desmoplakin (DSP) are a leading cause of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, a severe heart muscle disease characterized by fibrosis and life-threatening arrhythmias. Desmoplakin anchors the junctions that hold heart muscle cells together to the internal cytoskeleton, enabling the heart to withstand the force of each contraction. No targeted therapy exists, and DSP is too large for conventional gene replacement. Here we show, in explanted human hearts and in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes, that truncating DSP variants reduce desmoplakin RNA and protein, and that the resulting haploinsufficiency renders cardiomyocytes vulnerable to cell–cell adhesion failure under contractile stress, preceded by disruption of the cell membrane. Lowering contractile force with the myosin inhibitor mavacamten prevents this failure. Circumventing the size of DSP, CRISPR-based transcriptional activation of the endogenous gene restores desmoplakin expression and rescues adhesion. Haploinsufficiency is therefore the primary defect in DSP cardiomyopathy, and transcriptional activation offers a therapeutic strategy.

observations.text:
BackgroundWhether multi-agent large language model (LLM) pipelines help, add nothing, or underperform a single call may depend on the input and scoring contract rather than the architecture; these boundary conditions are unmapped.

MethodsWe compared a single direct call (Ax1), five personas in one context (P), and five isolated roles integrated by a moderator (MDT) across curated corpora (87 clinicopathological cases, 406 MedCaseReasoning cases, 392 replication vignettes) and two disjoint emergency cohorts from one repository (364 mixed-label encounters; a protocol-frozen 400-encounter disease-label-only replacement, one local serving stack). Scoring was judge-mediated top-k working-label matching. A completed factorial isolated the active ingredient; a symptom-permissive output-contract arm tested contract fit; three physicians rated discordant cases.

FindingsOn curated corpora MDT improved differential-list recall (top-3: +5{middle dot}5 points, p = 0{middle dot}0079; +3{middle dot}0, p = 0{middle dot}0079; +3{middle dot}3, p = 0{middle dot}0013) but not top-1 accuracy; the factorial attributed the gain to independent generation plus moderated synthesis, not personas. On emergency presentations the sign reversed: in the disease-label-only cohort Ax1 led MDT at every endpoint (top-3 -5{middle dot}2 points, 95% CI -8{middle dot}0 to -2{middle dot}4, p = 0{middle dot}0008), a second family reproduced it, and bridged cases excluded the serving stack. A symptom-permissive contract shrank the deficits point estimates by 52-75%, replacement-cohort intervals all spanning zero though remaining negative; the clause harmed no arm. Physician safety ratings were inconclusive (original-cohort gate missed; replacement-cohort rescue contrast unadjudicable, 95% CI -32{middle dot}7 to +2{middle dot}6).

InterpretationMulti-agent diagnostic gains are real but conditional: the sign of the effect tracks input genre, and its magnitude tracks output-contract fit. Curated-benchmark gains should not be extrapolated to first-contact emergency text, where role-based teams underperform a single call at seven-fold token cost. The reversal is label-level and judge-mediated; clinical safety is neither established nor excluded.

FundingNone.

Research in contextO_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyC_ST_ABSMulti-agent LLM diagnostic pipelines report gains, but specialist personas, independent generation, synthesis, and additional test-time compute are usually varied together, so the active ingredient is unidentified. Evaluation is concentrated on curated case reports, leaving performance on first-contact notes and working-diagnosis labels unclear, and no study has tested whether the output contract demanded of the model contributes to measured underperformance.

Added value of this studyAcross curated corpora and two disjoint emergency cohorts, we show the multi-agent effect is conditional and map two of its moderators. A completed factorial attributes the curated gain to independent generation plus moderated synthesis, not personas, and confines it to differential-list recall. The emergency deficit is established on a protocol-frozen cohort whose labels are all disease-level diagnoses, reproduced by a second model family on the same cases, and insensitive to the serving stack on bridged cases--so neither symptom-level labels nor the stack explains it. A symptom-permissive output contract closes the breadth component of the deficit while the ordering component persists. Physician safety ratings are inconclusive by design.

Implications of all the available evidenceGains measured on curated benchmarks should not be extrapolated to first-contact clinical text. Where multi-call designs are used on uncurated input, plain independent samples with a moderating call avoid the role-list penalty. An output contract permitting undifferentiated symptom-level entries is free--it harmed no arm--and is a defensible default wherever reference labels may be working diagnoses. Strategy selection by input, model, and endpoint remains a hypothesis requiring prospective evaluation, with independent emergency datasets and adequately powered safety studies.
observations.title: Multi-agent LLM diagnostic teams improve differential recall on curated cases and reverse on real emergency notes: a label-level reversal without a clinician-judged safety difference

observations.text: Protein coding variants span the gamut of structural and functional effects on proteins, and they have similarly heterogeneous effects on traits. Their functional effects can be predicted and categorized, particularly using machine learning models, and integrating these predictors benefits gene discovery. However, it remains unclear how well known structural features and predicted functional scores explain the heterogeneous effects of protein coding variants on human complex traits. We introduce the Kernel Allelic Series Model (KASM), which integrates multiple functional annotations to form a kernel describing how allelic effects within a gene covary. We apply it to exome data from 26 traits and 786,871 individuals from UK Biobank and All of Us, integrating 35 annotations describing protein structure and predicting allelic effects. We estimate that rare missense heritability is at least 1.27{+/-}0.09% on average, 1.83{+/-}0.11% under our most flexible model, exceeding pLoF heritability (0.87{+/-}0.05%) and far exceeding missense burden heritability as previously estimated (0.54{+/-}0.04%). AlphaMissense is the single most enriched missense predictor, but a composite score doubles its enrichment. A series of structural features is enriched for heritability, from amino acid chemical features and structural motifs to residue contacts and protein-protein interaction interfaces. Examining pairs of variants, we find that most missense effects are modestly correlated, but an exception is when residues are close in 3D structure but distant in 1D sequence; such pairs also covary across species. Finally, we analyze individual genes and identify gene-specific enrichments, like a 95-fold enrichment among PIEZO1 hydrogen bond residues, that nominate functional hypotheses.

observations.text: Perception is often described as Bayesian inference, where precise expectations are assumed to dominate perception by pulling estimates strongly toward their mean. However, this effect may reverse when the hidden cause of the sensory input is unknown and must itself be inferred among competing alternatives. We tested this prediction in a voice-recognition task in which listeners learned three voices of speakers that differed in precision, defined as the inverse variance of the acoustic features of their voices. When classifying ambiguous utterances, listeners across five experiments systematically favored speakers with lower-precision, i.e., more variable voices, an effect that was strongest under high sensory ambiguity and amplified by explicit knowledge of speaker variance. Computational modeling showed that listeners tracked and used idiosyncratic, speaker-specific precision estimates that increased with learning accuracy and were stable across sessions. These findings show that precision does not simply determine the strength with which perceptual estimates are drawn toward a prediction; when the hidden cause must be inferred among competing alternatives, it also determines which prediction is favored. Our results identify precision as a critical determinant of perceptual inference when multiple hidden causes provide competing predictions about a stimulus.
observations.title: When precise expectations lose: Precision and Competition Among Hidden Causes in Voice Recognition

observations.text:
Stroke is a leading cause of mortality and disability in Uganda, with a prevalence of approximately 2.5% and a 25-30% 30-day mortality rate, exacerbated by limited access to predictive tools and advanced diagnostics. Machine learning (ML) offers potential for early stroke risk stratification, but its application in resource-constrained settings like Uganda requires tailored models and rigorous performance evaluation, as well as assessment of misclassification patterns. This study aimed to develop and internally validate an ML-based predictive model for stroke using clinical and socio-demographic characteristics among patients at Mulago National Referral Hospital (MNRH) and residents of Wakiso District, Uganda, identify key predictors and assess misclassification patterns to enhance targeted prevention.

A retrospective case-control study utilized secondary data from 1,016 participants (254 stroke cases, 762 controls) across three prior studies conducted between 2006 and 2015. Eight ML algorithms were evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation, with performance metrics including accuracy, sensitivity, positive predictive value, F1-score, and area under receiver operator characteristics curve (AU-ROC). McNemars test compared model classification performance of the top 2 models. Feature importance identified key predictors, and misclassification patterns were analyzed using classification matrix and line graphs.

The Random Forest (RF) model achieved the highest performance (95.18% accuracy, 90.10% F1-score, 97% AU-ROC). McNemars test confirmed RFs superior classification (p=0.01). Age, systolic blood pressure, total cholesterol, and waist-hip ratio were the top drivers of RF stroke predictions. RF misclassified 8.3% of stroke cases and 3.3% of non-stroke cases, due to overlaps in risk profiles (e.g., lower cholesterol, systolic blood pressure and age in false negatives).

The RF model demonstrates strong potential for stroke risk prediction in Uganda, leveraging routine data to prioritize high-risk individuals. Misclassification analysis highlights areas for model refinement, supporting its potential for integration into clinical workflows for early intervention and stroke prevention in resource-limited settings. Future external validation across diverse populations is recommended.

metadata.summary: Muscle LIM Protein (MLP) is a key component of the cardiomyocyte Z disc that is essential for sarcomere integrity and cardiac homeostasis.  Loss of MLP function results in (cardio)myopathy phenotypes in animal models and is associated with inherited cardiomyopathies in humans. Here, we identify MLP as an evolutionarily conserved non-canonical RNA-binding protein and uncover RNA binding as a previously unrecognized mechanism involved in its cytoskeletal association. Using enhanced RNA interactome capture together with complementary biochemical approaches, we demonstrate direct RNA binding by MLP and map two short RNA-binding motifs adjacent to its LIM domains. Disrupting these motifs markedly reduces RNA association, including residues associated with cardiomyopathies. Mechanistically, RNA is required for MLP’s interactions with cytoskeletal proteins, and for the formation of higher-order MLP-containing assemblies. Consistently, RNA-binding-deficient MLP mutants exhibit impaired interactions with cytoskeletal proteins and reduced cytoskeletal retention. Our findings reveal the importance of RNA binding for the formation of MLP assemblies, and support the emerging role of RNA as a co-factor in the organization of macromolecular complexes, with potential relevance to human disease.

IntroductionDespite the significant burden of Shigellosis, routine surveillance systems in resource-limited settings lack predictive capabilities to guide proactive public health responses. Consequently, we developed and evaluated the accuracy, uncertainty and computational cost of multi-horizon forecasting models for Shigella incidence among children <5 years in rural western Kenya using 16-year longitudinal incidence time-series.

MethodsWe estimated monthly Shigella incidence using data from three pediatric enteric studies (2008- 2024), supplemented with Kenya Health Information System during inter-study gaps. Incidence estimates incorporated sampling, healthcare-seeking, stool-testing, and pathogen-specific weights, with bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals. Predictors included Google Trends health-related indicators, climate, temporal trends, and seasonality. Forecasts at 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons were evaluated using rolling-origin validation. Following horizon-specific predictor selection using Boruta, 14 state-space, machine-learning, and hybrid models were compared using point-forecast and probabilistic metrics, bootstrap confidence intervals, and Model Confidence Sets. Adaptive conformal prediction recalibrated prediction intervals, while Shapley Additive exPlanations assessed predictor contributions.

ResultsMean monthly Shigella incidence was 2.51 per 100 child-years (standard deviation=1.85). Shigella dynamics in Kenya can be forecast beyond seasonal persistence alone for up to six months reducing absolute errors by [~] 33%. However, optimal model architectures and predictor sets shift systematically across forecasting horizons. Temporal trend and recent incidence were the dominant predictors, while predictor importance shifted with forecast horizon toward syndromic, pharmaceutical, seasonal, and lagged environmental signals. Extreme Gradient Boosting performed best at 1 month (Root mean squared error [RMSE]=1.86), remained competitive at 3 months (RMSE=1.89), whereas exponential smoothing (ETS) performed best at 6 months (RMSE=2.05). Forecast accuracy declined with increasing horizon. ETS and TBATS provided the best-calibrated prediction intervals, whereas machine-learning models generally under-covered. Model Confidence Sets demonstrated horizon-dependent model distinguishability.

ConclusionHorizon-specific model selection balancing predictive accuracy, uncertainty calibration, and computational feasibility could strengthen operational early warning systems for shigellosis.

Author SummaryShigella infections remain an important cause of illness among young children in low-resource settings, yet public health systems often lack tools to anticipate changes in disease burden before they occur. Early warning systems that can reliably predict future Shigella incidence could help health authorities plan surveillance, allocate resources, and prepare for periods of increased transmission. We used 16 years of data from children <5 years in rural western Kenya to develop and compare different approaches for forecasting monthly Shigella incidence 1-, 3-, and 6-months ahead. We combined disease surveillance data with information on seasonal patterns, weather, and health-related internet searches. We found that Shigella incidence could be predicted beyond what would be expected from seasonal patterns alone, with useful forecasts possible up to six months ahead. However, the best forecasting approach depended on how far into the future predictions were required. Machine-learning methods provided the most accurate short-term predictions, while simpler statistical models performed better for longer-term forecasts and provided more reliable estimates of uncertainty. These findings highlight the importance of selecting forecasting methods according to the intended prediction horizon and operational requirements. Such approaches could strengthen early warning and preparedness for childhood Shigella infections in resource-limited settings.
observations.title: Towards Early Warning Systems for Shigellosis in Africa: Multi-Horizon Forecasting of Incidence in Rural Western Kenya Using Statistical State-Space and Machine Learning Models
